title: Interview: shopping list behavior
lead: Decide how the list is generated, displayed and cleared.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The list is the main shared surface, so its behavior has to match how the household actually orders (e.g., typing items into a store's pickup app by hand).

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. Aggregation: sum the same item across recipes in compatible units (recommended); show which recipes need it?
2. Rounding: show recipe quantities ("3 tbsp chili powder") or a purchase hint ("1 jar")?
3. Category order: per ADR 0019; is one order enough, or one per store?
4. Checked items: hide immediately, or strike through until "clear"?
5. When does a list "reset": after the order is placed (a manual "Ordered" button) (recommended), or weekly?
6. Concurrency: two phones editing at once. Is polling every few seconds enough (recommended), or is live updating needed?
7. Free-text items (not canonical): allowed (recommended)?

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Ask the questions with recommendations.
2. Write ADR 0020; record the raw answers in `local/` (not committed).
3. Update the list generation and list UI slices (`slicer edit`).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - ADR 0020 covers aggregation, rounding, ordering, clearing and concurrency.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
